Danielle —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, attaching a concise MAP proposal that folds the performance evaluation into the mutual action plan so we can close on sizing and procurement in the next 3 weeks. High level asks and planned outputs below: 

- Objectives: validate p50/p95 latency, TTFT (time-to-first-token), steady-state throughput at target concurrency, and failure/fallback behavior across A100 / H100 / L40S with MIG vs full-GPU profiles.
- Deliverables: CSV of raw run results (attached), annotated charts (png), and a recommended fleet mix + cost delta for 6/12/24-month commit windows.
- Test matrix (short):
  * Models: customer sample gen / internal 13B and 70B proxies (same tokenizer).
  * Sequence lengths: 64, 256, 1024 tokens.
  * Concurrency windows: 1, 8, 32, 128 concurrent sessions.
  * Metrics: TTFT, p50/p90/p95 latency per token & per-response, tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, mem pressure, KV cache hit rate.
  * Variants: quantized FP16 vs Q4 variants where feasible; batching sizes 1..16.
- Environments: hosted dedicated capacity with isolated VPC, drivers stack (CUDA 12.x, cuDNN matched), and Redwood runtime v3.7.

Can you confirm:
1) A 48-hour window next week to run the full matrix against your sample workload?
2) Who on procurement we should loop in (and whether a PO or SOW is preferred up front)?
3) Any additional security docs you need; we can push SOC2 artifacts and an IP addendum if required.

Attachments: map-performance-results.csv (seed runs), h100-vs-a100-l40s-chart.png, map-draft-SOW.docx

Next steps: if you confirm the test window I’ll post a HubSpot MAP with milestones and link DocuSign for the SOW.

Danielle / Jason —

Confirmed for Feb 23–24. Below is the proposed tactical runbook and the exact test matrix we’ll execute in order (short, reproducible steps). I’m also attaching the CSV of seed runs we ran in our lab — this will be our baseline for expected ranges.

Planned runbook excerpt (high level):
1) Baseline smoke: single session, batch=1, seq=64 on A100/H100/L40S full-GPU to validate environment and tokenizer parity.
2) Cold-start TTFT: fresh runtime, measure time from request receipt to first token emitted (server-side timestamp minus client receive); repeat 30x, report median and p95.
3) Warm-cache TTFT: load KV cache by executing N warmup prompts (configurable), then run same requests 100x.
4) Steady-state throughput: ramp concurrency in steps (1 -> 8 -> 32 -> 128) holding model and seq length constant; measure tokens/sec and GPU util.
5) MIG runs: repeat steps 1–4 on 1/2/4-way MIG slices (where supported) to characterize efficiency vs fragmentation.
6) Quantization and batching sweep: run Q4 and FP16 variants across batch sizes 1/2/4/8/16.

Key measurement notes:
- TTFT will be measured server-side at the moment of first token generation; we’ll also include end-to-end observed TTFT from a simulated client to capture network/streaming overhead.
- We’ll report per-run traces, aggregated latency distributions, and a cost-normalized throughput chart (tokens/sec per GPU-hour).

Estimated timeline inside MAP:
- Feb 16–19: MAP & SOW finalization (DocuSign link provided after procurement confirms PO path).
- Feb 23–24: Lab runs (48h).
- Feb 25–26: Analysis & recommendation write-up; fleet-sizing proposal and cost scenarios delivered.

Attachments referenced: map-performance-results.csv, h100-vs-a100-l40s-chart.png, map-draft-SOW.docx

Danielle / Neha —

Quick technical notes from the runtime team so expectations are aligned for the run results:

- H100 wins at low-latency single-session workloads for models with larger memory needs due to better Tensor cores for fp16 and larger L2 caches; expect p50 gains ~10–25% vs A100 for short sequences.
- L40S tends to provide better cost-normalized throughput for high token-rate applications (high batching) due to cheaper hourly cost; ideal when you can batch to >=4.
- MIG: efficient but fragmented. For predictable per-customer isolation and high-concurrency small-session workloads, 2-way MIG hit rate is attractive. For throughput-heavy steady streams, full-GPU profiles outperform MIG due to inter-slice communication overhead.
- KV cache effects: with long context (1k tokens) cache hit rate dramatically reduces compute — measure cold vs warm carefully and report eviction rates.

Operational recommendation (preliminary):
- Start with a mixed pool: H100 for latency-sensitive endpoints (canary + small-batch webhooks) + L40S cluster for bulk throughput tasks; reserve a small A100 pool if customer needs cross-cloud portability (some partners still have A100 only).
- If procurement prefers fewer SKUs, prioritize H100 + L40S over A100.

I’ll join the run window to watch hot paths and annotate traces.
